# Mixxx agent backend

This local Python service manages a music library, plans policy-compliant DJ
sessions, executes two-deck queues through a native bridge, and records command
results. It is separate from Mixxx's C++ build and uses the existing AI DJ
project's FastAPI and `/api/v1` conventions. It is not a drop-in replacement for
that project's djay API; its adapter must be updated before connecting it.

The native C++ bridge is implemented in `src/agent/` and enabled explicitly with
Mixxx's `--agent-bridge` option. The ChatGPT plugin is not yet packaged.
Without a connected bridge, library and planning operations work, status reports
`connected: false`, and playback commands return `BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE`. Tests use
an explicit simulated bridge; normal startup never simulates Mixxx playback.
Apple Music catalogue access and subscription streaming are not implemented.

## Install and run

Use Python 3.11 or newer. From the repository root, run each command separately:

```shell
python3 -m venv backend/.venv
backend/.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r backend/requirements-dev.lock
backend/.venv/bin/python -m pip install --no-deps -e backend
backend/.venv/bin/mixxx-backend --music-dir "$HOME/Music"
```

The lock file pins the runtime and development dependencies used for validation.
Repeat `--music-dir` to allow other directories. With no music roots configured,
registration is denied. Supported file extensions are MP3, FLAC, WAV, AIFF, M4A,
OGG and Opus; successful registration also requires readable audio metadata.
DRM-protected subscription downloads cannot be registered as playable files.

The service binds to `127.0.0.1:8765` with one worker. `--port` and `--data-dir`
override the defaults. Only one process may own a data directory. Environment
alternatives are `MIXXX_DATA_DIR` and `MIXXX_MUSIC_ROOTS` (colon-separated paths
on macOS/Linux, semicolon-separated on Windows). Set `MIXXX_DATA_DIR` for both
the server and request utility when using a custom directory.

The backend CLI generates `.data/mixxx-bridge.json`, containing the loopback URL
and the token-file path, without embedding the token. Launch the rebuilt app in
a separate terminal at the repository root:

```shell
mkdir -p "$PWD/build/user-settings"
./build/mixxx --resource-path "$PWD/res" --settings-path "$PWD/build/user-settings" --agent-bridge "$PWD/backend/.data/mixxx-bridge.json"
```

When using a custom data directory, pass its `mixxx-bridge.json` instead.
The bridge is disabled by default. Invalid configurations are logged and leave
Mixxx running without agent control. Networking runs asynchronously on the Qt
application thread and file hashes are checked in a worker, outside the audio
thread. The bridge must be explicitly enabled again on the next app launch.

Startup creates `backend/.data/` with private directory permissions, SQLite
storage and two distinct token files: `api-token` for clients and `bridge-token`
for the native bridge. Requests use `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Tokens stay
in local files and are never printed by the CLI. Keep this service on loopback;
it is not configured as an internet-facing or multi-user server.

## Try the API

In a second terminal at the repository root:

```shell
backend/.venv/bin/mixxx-api GET /api/v1/health
backend/.venv/bin/mixxx-api GET /api/v1/mixxx/status
backend/.venv/bin/mixxx-api POST /api/v1/tracks --json '{"path":"/absolute/path/to/song.mp3"}'
backend/.venv/bin/mixxx-api GET '/api/v1/tracks?q=song'
```

The request utility reads the API token itself. Replace the example path with
a file inside an allowed music root. Registration extracts title, artist and
duration, identifies exact file content by SHA-256, and records size/mtime.
Re-register changed files. Identical content is deduplicated. This is not an
acoustic fingerprint: transcoded versions can have different identities.

`PUT /api/v1/tracks/{id}/metadata` replaces the editable metadata, for example:

```json
{
  "title": "Song title",
  "artist": "Artist name",
  "language": "english",
  "explicit": false,
  "bpm": 120,
  "camelot_key": "8A",
  "energy": 6
}
```

BPM, language, content rating, key and energy are operator-supplied; this backend
does not perform acoustic analysis or invent missing values. Session planning
requires known BPM, excludes explicit and unrated content by default, and checks
file availability, blocked tracks/artists, duplicate content, artist cooldowns,
language streaks, and requested runtime after transition overlaps. Language
weights sum to 1 and are balanced by track count with a one-track rounding
tolerance per language. Plans report coverage and blockers; insufficient plans
cannot start. The planner is deterministic and greedy, so it may report
insufficient coverage even if another ordering could satisfy the rules.

## API routes

All paths below have the `/api/v1` prefix. Everything except `GET /health`
requires the corresponding bearer token. The authenticated OpenAPI document is
at `GET /openapi.json`; it defines request types, limits and required fields.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/health`, `/capabilities`, `/mixxx/status` | Service health, supported features and observed state |
| POST / GET | `/tracks` | Register one local file / search and paginate registered tracks |
| GET | `/tracks/{id}` | Track metadata and current availability |
| PUT | `/tracks/{id}/metadata` | Replace operator-reviewed metadata |
| POST / GET | `/dj/sessions` | Create / list sessions |
| GET | `/dj/sessions/active`, `/dj/sessions/{id}` | Active or selected session and playback state |
| PUT | `/dj/sessions/{id}/settings?revision=N` | Replace rules with revision protection |
| GET / POST | `/dj/sessions/{id}/plan` | Preview / save a complete generated plan |
| PUT | `/dj/sessions/{id}/queue` | Replace the queue with validated track IDs |
| GET | `/dj/sessions/{id}/coverage`, `/dj/sessions/{id}/upcoming` | Coverage / planned queue |
| POST | `/dj/sessions/{id}/start` | Start orchestration using an approved revision |
| POST | `/dj/sessions/{id}/end` | End orchestration; does not stop audible playback |
| POST | `/dj/commands`, `/dj/sessions/{id}/commands` | Submit an explicit deck/mixer command |
| GET | `/dj/commands/{id}` | Inspect delivery and confirmation |
| POST | `/dj/commands/{id}/reconcile` | Explicitly resolve an uncertain command |
| GET | `/events?after=N&limit=100` | Read the persisted audit stream |

Create a session with `{"name":"Party","settings":{"duration_minutes":60}}`.
Queue replacement uses `{"revision":0,"track_ids":["registered-id", "..."]}`.
Plan saving and starting use `{"revision":N}`. Successful queue/rule changes and
start increment the revision; retrieve the latest session before editing it.
Only draft/ready sessions are editable. Only one running or suspended session
may own playback. End a suspended session explicitly before starting another.

Starting activates the scheduler, which loads deck 1, routes the crossfader,
sets deck volume, starts playback, preloads deck 2 and requests native
transitions near the end of each track. It stops both decks when the planned
runtime is reached. Timing uses observed normalized position and source-file
duration; it is approximate, especially if playback speed changes. Beat-level
scheduling, ramps, synchronization and audio processing belong in the native
bridge. This service never executes DSP or waits for an LLM inside the audio
thread. A saved queue is a plan; `runtime.played_track_ids` records tracks whose
start commands were confirmed. It is not evidence of full-track listening.

## Commands and confirmation

Every command submission requires an `Idempotency-Key` header. Retrying the same
key and body returns the same command. Reusing it for another body returns 409.
Controls are serialized; resolve an outstanding uncertain command before issuing
another. `stop` can preempt queued work and suspends session orchestration.

| `command_type` | Required additional fields | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `load_track` | `deck`, `track_id` | Load a registered file onto a paused deck |
| `set_playing` | `deck`, `playing` | Explicit play/pause state |
| `stop` | None | Stop both decks and cancel native pending transitions |
| `seek` | `deck`, `value` | Normalized position 0..1 |
| `set_bpm` | `deck`, `value` | Absolute BPM 20..300 |
| `set_sync` | `deck`, `enabled` | Explicit sync state |
| `set_volume` | `deck`, `value` | Channel volume 0..1 |
| `set_crossfader` | `value` | Crossfader -1 (deck 1) to +1 (deck 2) |
| `set_eq` | `deck`, `band`, `value` | Low/mid/high gain 0..2; 1 is neutral |
| `set_effect` | `effect_unit`, `enabled` | Existing effect unit 1..4 enabled state |
| `transition` | `deck`, `duration_ms` | Transition to a loaded paused destination, 0..30000 ms |

Unknown fields, non-finite numbers, toggles, arbitrary control names and
out-of-range values are rejected. During a session, manual controls other than
stop are blocked; the scheduler owns the decks until orchestration ends.

Commands progress from `queued` to `sent` and then `confirmed` or `rejected`.
Unsent timeouts become `expired`; sent timeouts become `uncertain`. Delivery
alone never confirms playback. On restart, queued work is cancelled, sent work
becomes uncertain, bridge telemetry is invalidated, and running sessions are
suspended. No commands are automatically replayed and no session automatically
resumes after a restart or disconnection. Ending/suspending orchestration does
not guarantee already-dispatched native work has stopped.

Reconciliation accepts `{"outcome":"confirmed"}` only if fresh telemetry
matches the command, or `{"outcome":"not_executed"}` as an explicit operator
assertion. These results are labelled `operator_reconciliation`, not native
acknowledgements. Neither native state nor an acknowledgement proves audible
output through the selected sound device.

## Native bridge protocol v1

These routes use **bridge-token**, not api-token. See
[BRIDGE_PROTOCOL.md](BRIDGE_PROTOCOL.md) for execution and acknowledgement rules.
HTTP polling is intentional: a C++ client can use Qt Network without adding a
WebSocket dependency. There is no arbitrary-code or shell-execution endpoint.

## Validation

From the repository root:

```shell
backend/.venv/bin/python -m pytest backend/tests -q
backend/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check backend
backend/.venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check backend
backend/.venv/bin/python -m pip check
```

Tests cover real temporary WAV registration, policy/coverage checks, revision
conflicts, simulated native command acknowledgements, two-deck session
execution, isolation, expired commands and restart/disconnection handling.
Native C++ bridge tests are included in `mixxx-test`. Run the targeted tests
after building Mixxx:

```shell
./build/mixxx-test --gtest_filter='AgentBridgeTest.*:MixxxTest.AgentConfig*:PlayerManagerTest.AgentBridge*' --resource-path "$PWD/res"
```

The optional localhost integration harness starts a temporary backend and a
native test fixture with real Mixxx controls, library loading and engine
processing. It loads generated WAV files, plays, transitions and stops, without
opening a sound device or changing the user's running app:

```shell
backend/.venv/bin/python backend/tools/native_smoke.py
```

Neither these tests nor bridge telemetry establish audible output, controller
behavior, UI rendering, or ChatGPT plugin installation. Testing on a real DJ
setup remains necessary before live use.
